# Candidate absorber materials
- Absorber-F1: dense alloy with a short radiation length.
- Absorber-F3: dense alloy, different composition.
- Absorber-F2: standard structural absorber.
All three can be machined to the required plate tolerances.

# Cooling
Water cooling at 18 C. The heat load is dominated by the front-end electronics.

# Meeting notes 2026-05-14
The mechanical support design was reviewed and is compatible with every candidate absorber.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 5 mm plates)
Energy resolution for 100 GeV electrons: Absorber-F1 3.2%, Absorber-F3 3.9%, Absorber-F2 5.1%.

input.justification: Absorber-F1 with 5 mm plate thickness achieves the best energy resolution of 3.172% at 100 GeV among all tested configurations. This was determined through systematic simulation of all three candidate absorber materials (F1, F2, F3) across plate thicknesses from 2-10 mm. The optimal thickness of 5 mm represents the minimum in the resolution curve for F1, with resolution degrading at both thinner plates (3.665% at 3mm, 3.712% at 2mm) and thicker plates (3.374% at 6mm, increasing to 4.699% at 10mm). Absorber-F1 at 5mm outperforms the best configurations of F3 (3.922% at 4mm) and F2 (5.045% at 4mm) by significant margins. This recommendation assumes all candidate materials meet the radiation safety requirements, as all three are listed as official candidates in the project documentation.
